task_read: An extremely large, long-horizon greenfield build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + JSON API + SPA + WebSocket collab) whose centerpiece is an Excel-365 formula engine with ~150 functions, dynamic-array spill, dependency-graph topological recompute under hard performance budgets, plus XLSX round-trip, pivots, conditional formatting, locale input, data validation, iterative calc, and goal seek. Crucially the exact wire contract is UNDER-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing first-party client (/dev_tests/helpers.py), and grading is on a much larger hidden suite than the provided smoke tests. This demands heavy, sustained, well-sequenced meta-work: deep upfront contract discovery, aggressive milestone decomposition across dozens of subsystems, self-built verification against Excel semantics and perf targets, continuous progress tracking, and repeated course-correction as design assumptions (library choice, engine architecture) meet reality.

dimensions.name: Contract discovery & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Reverse-engineering the exact wire shapes and semantics from /dev_tests/helpers.py and run.sh, probing the runtime, and inferring the huge implicit Excel-365 contract before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shape (ids, cell kinds, spill fields, patch/fill/sort bodies, listing envelope) is defined ONLY by the existing client; guessing it means every endpoint fails the hidden suite. Excel function semantics and error propagation are also an implicit spec that rewards reading real references over improvisation.

anchors.0: Starts coding endpoints/engine from the prose spec alone; never opens helpers.py or the dev_tests.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, copies a couple of obvious shapes, but leaves most request/response shapes and cell discriminators guessed.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh carefully, extracts the concrete JSON shapes (workbook ids, cell kind discriminator, spill/spill_range fields, patch/fill/sort/filter bodies, listing envelope) and builds to them before large-scale coding.
anchors.8: Systematically derives the full contract from the client — every helper call mapped to an endpoint and shape — AND grounds ambiguous Excel semantics (spill rules, error precedence, criteria/wildcards, XLSX OOXML structure) in deliberate reference-checking; records the derived contract so later work stays consistent.
anchors.10: Sustained, self-correcting discovery: exhaustively maps the client contract, revisits helpers.py whenever a new subsystem is touched, proactively resolves under-specified corners (locale canonicalization, iterative-calc convergence, presence/backfill semantics) by cross-referencing the client's actual usage and Excel ground truth, and continuously feeds findings back into the design rather than discovering shape mismatches late.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & milestone sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking a sprawling product into an ordered hierarchy of independently-verifiable subsystems (persistence/API skeleton → dependency graph → formula parser/evaluator → functions → spill → collab → XLSX → analyst surfaces → SPA) with a dependency-aware build order.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of loosely-coupled features on top of a shared core (parser, dep-graph, recompute). Wrong ordering (e.g. building pivots before the evaluator works, or the SPA before the API stabilizes) causes rework and stalls; a foundation-first order lets each layer be validated before the next depends on it.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no milestones, features tackled in arbitrary order.
anchors.3: A flat to-do list of features with no dependency ordering or done-criteria.
anchors.5: Clear phased plan that puts the health endpoint/persistence and core engine (parse → dep-graph → recompute) before dependent features, with rough milestones.
anchors.8: Dependency-aware milestone hierarchy where each milestone has an explicit done-check and unlocks the next; risky/foundational core (topological recompute, spill, XLSX value parity) is sequenced early and features are batched sensibly.
anchors.10: Masterful decomposition that isolates the highest-risk shared machinery first, defines crisp exit criteria per milestone, sequences the ~150-function catalog and perf/collab/analyst layers to minimize rework, and is explicitly revisited/re-ordered as the true dependency structure emerges.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — running the live server against helpers.py flows, testing function/error/spill semantics, XLSX round-trip via openpyxl, and perf benchmarks — knowing dev_tests is non-exhaustive and grading is on a hidden suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The provided suite explicitly under-covers; passing it proves little. Excel-value correctness, error sentinels, spill, XLSX parity against LibreOffice ground truth, and the hard latency budgets (100k-cell import <30s, 5k dependents <2s) are only caught by verification the agent builds itself.

anchors.0: No verification, or asserts success without ever running the server.
anchors.3: Runs /dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke suite as done.
anchors.5: Runs the server, exercises core flows through the real API, and spot-checks function outputs and one XLSX round-trip beyond the smoke tests.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks for the risky invariants the smoke suite misses — error propagation, spill/ghost rejection, XLSX round-trip via openpyxl against expected values, and at least rough perf timing against the stated budgets — and uses failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Designs a layered verification regime: Excel-semantics oracles for functions/errors, round-trip and cross-tool (openpyxl) parity checks, collab op/seq/backfill assertions, and explicit perf benchmarks against every stated budget — re-run as regressions across milestones, so correctness is demonstrated rather than assumed on the hidden suite.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a huge feature surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which subsystems/functions/endpoints are done, in-progress, or untouched across a very long horizon, and detecting stalls or circular debugging.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and a dozen subsystems, it is easy to lose the plot — over-polishing one area while whole surfaces (locale, goal seek, conditional formatting) are missing, or re-debugging the same recompute bug in circles. Accurate coverage tracking is what sustains progress to the end.

anchors.0: No sense of remaining scope; drifts between features and forgets whole surfaces.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unimplemented areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a running checklist of subsystems/functions and updates it as items complete, giving a usable done-vs-remaining picture.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, regularly-updated status of the full surface (functions, endpoints, error cases, perf, collab, SPA), and notices when it is stuck on one item too long and reallocates.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate horizon tracking: coverage state is kept current across all subsystems, stalls/thrashing are detected early and explicitly named, effort is rebalanced toward untouched high-value surfaces, and nothing large is silently dropped by the end.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on architecture & approach
dimensions.description: Revising design decisions — library-vs-hand-rolled formula evaluation and OOXML I/O, engine architecture, recompute strategy — when they hit correctness, performance, or contract walls, rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Big early bets (which library evaluates formulas, how the dep-graph and spill are modeled, how XLSX is emitted) will collide with Excel semantics, the hidden contract, or the perf budgets. Detecting a falsified assumption and re-architecting early is the difference between a working product and a dead end.

anchors.0: Commits to an initial approach and never revisits it even as tests/perf fail repeatedly.
anchors.3: Makes local patches to symptoms but never questions a failing underlying design choice.
anchors.5: When a subsystem clearly fails (wrong values, perf miss, contract mismatch), backs up and changes the approach for that piece.
anchors.8: Actively watches for falsified assumptions, diagnoses root cause (e.g. eager vs dirty-only recompute failing the 2s budget, a library that can't round-trip conditional formatting), and re-architects deliberately rather than piling on workarounds.
anchors.10: Treats the design as a living hypothesis: anticipates likely failure points, validates risky bets early with spikes, and when reality diverges performs clean, well-reasoned pivots (engine model, library choice, spill/collab strategy) that are propagated consistently through plan, code, and verification.

dimensions.name: Fidelity to exact Excel/wire semantics as an explicit target
dimensions.description: Treating precise conformance — exact error sentinels and their precedence, spill/ghost rules, locale canonicalization, deterministic pivot/header ordering, iterative-calc convergence math, cell-by-cell value parity — as a first-class objective rather than settling for approximately-right behavior.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The verifier grades values cell-by-cell against LibreOffice ground truth and checks named error types and status codes; 'close enough' Excel behavior silently fails the hidden suite. This exactness bar cuts across all subsystems and is a distinct meta-work concern from generic verification: it is about how demanding a correctness standard the agent holds itself to.

anchors.0: Implements features to 'roughly Excel-like' behavior with no attention to exact sentinels, ordering, or parity.
anchors.3: Gets happy-path values right but is careless about error names/status codes, precedence, and determinism.
anchors.5: Deliberately matches the documented error sentinels/HTTP statuses and core semantics for the common cases.
anchors.8: Holds an explicit exactness standard: verifies error precedence, spill-target rejection, locale round-tripping to canonical en-US, deterministic pivot ordering, and value parity on representative hard cases.
anchors.10: Systematically drives toward full ground-truth parity: treats every semantic corner (edge-case error propagation, iterative fixed-point settling, XLSX numFmt/style/CF fidelity) as a checkable target and closes gaps against an Excel/LibreOffice oracle rather than assuming conformance.
